llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is overwhelmingly consistent with a common-path fibre DGD/PMD rise. At essentially the same onset, many independent 200G receivers show an approximately 64–65 unit DGD increase, elevated pre-FEC BER, OTU_LOF/SD, and widespread working-path failures or protection switches, while optical power, OSNR, and amplifier telemetry remain unchanged; this strongly excludes a cut, loss increase, amplifier failure, or individual client/line-card fault. The available observations do not isolate which particular shared span is responsible.

proposals.rationale: The simultaneous large DGD increases and BER/LOF effects across numerous receivers are the direct signature of excessive PMD on a common upstream fibre span. Unchanged power, OSNR, and amplifier measurements support DGD rather than attenuation or equipment gain failure, although the exact shared span cannot be distinguished.

A polarization transient on a shared span could simultaneously disturb coherent receivers without changing power or OSNR. It is much less likely because the measured DGD step is large and the resulting service failures persist, whereas SOP transients are normally millisecond events causing only brief errors.

Mechanical stress on a common, possibly aerial, span could induce polarization changes and thereby trigger the DGD event. However, this mode normally produces a brief power excursion, and the scoped power monitors saw no change.

A shifted WSS passband at the common S08 ROADM could degrade quality while leaving channel power approximately normal. It is weakly supported because the fault is defined per channel and would not naturally produce nearly identical DGD jumps on many independent channels and receivers.

proposals.rationale: Receiver-local degradation could account for LOF and BER at one line interface. It cannot plausibly explain the synchronous matching changes at many other receivers and the broad service impact.
